results.summary: This project implements a 4x4 structural array multiplier in Verilog that takes two 4-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit product. It is tested with a Cocotb testbench that applies various input combinations and checks the output against expected values. The design uses only the Tiny Tapeout pins and requires no external hardware. It appears to be an educational exercise in structural digital design, with detailed documentation of the partial product generation and summation process.

This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier implemented in Verilog, using AND gates and full adders to compute the 8-bit product of two 4-bit inputs. The design is purely combinational and can be tested by applying input values to the pins and observing the output. No external hardware is required. The documentation includes example test cases and a brief explanation of the structural approach, suggesting it is an educational project.

This project is a 4x4 array multiplier that generates and sums partial products to produce an 8-bit output from two 4-bit inputs. The documentation explains the general operation of an array multiplier but does not provide specific implementation details or test results. Testing involves applying binary inputs and verifying the output against expected multiplication results. No external hardware is needed. The design is likely an educational exercise, but the documentation is somewhat generic and lacks project-specific details.

This design implements an 8-bit ripple adder and an accumulator register, intended as components for a basic 8-bit CPU. The adder supports two's complement addition and subtraction, and provides zero and carry flags. The accumulator stores the adder output and can drive the bus via tri-state buffers. The design is part of a larger project and requires no external hardware beyond the Tiny Tapeout pins.

This project is a 4-bit ALU that performs arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and logical operations (AND, OR, NOT, XOR) on two 4-bit inputs. The operation is selected by a 3-bit opcode, and the ALU outputs an 8-bit result along with zero and carry flags. Testing is done by applying the appropriate opcode and inputs. The design is educational and requires no external hardware.

This project is a simple ring oscillator implemented by instantiating a sky130 inv_2 inverter ring in Verilog. It provides a single output pin for the oscillator signal. The documentation is minimal, consisting only of the title and one-line description, with no testing details or external hardware requirements. It is likely an experiment to characterize oscillator behavior in the sky130 process.

This project implements multiple ring oscillators using sky130 inv_2 inverter rings, with various output frequencies and PWM signals. The pins include inputs for PWM configuration and outputs for oscillator and PWM signals. The documentation is sparse, providing only a one-line description and pin names, with no detailed explanation or test procedure. It appears to be an experimental design for on-chip oscillator characterization.

This project is a sky130 inv_2 ring oscillator with an externally selectable length, allowing the oscillator frequency to be tuned via tap inputs. It provides eight output pins, likely for observing different taps or buffered outputs. The documentation is minimal, with only a one-line description and pin names, and no testing details. It is an experimental design for oscillator characterization.

This project implements three adaptive leaky integrate-and-fire (ALIF) neurons in Verilog. It receives an 8-bit input current, processes it through the LIF model with adaptive threshold, and outputs spike signals for each neuron along with the internal state of neuron 1. The design requires no external hardware and can be tested by applying input currents and monitoring spike outputs and state variables. The documentation describes the neuron model and testing approach, but the one-line description is marked TODO.

This project is a low-voltage operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) implemented in an analog process. It has three analog pins: one output (Vo) and two inputs (VA, VB). The documentation is very brief, stating only that it amplifies transconductance and has high output impedance, and suggests testing with a function generator. No external hardware is used. The design is notable for being an analog block in a digital-oriented shuttle.
